title: Sort Array by Increasing Frequency
statement: Sort values by increasing frequency; ties are ordered by decreasing numeric value.
explanation: Count each value, then sort by (frequency ascending, value descending).

title: Check If Two String Arrays are Equivalent
statement: Return true when concatenating each word array produces the same string.
explanation: Join each array's strings and compare the results.

title: Richest Customer Wealth
statement: Return the largest sum among all customer account rows.
explanation: Compute each customer's row sum and take the maximum.

title: Goal Parser Interpretation
statement: Decode G, (), and (al) as G, o, and al respectively.
explanation: Replace the longer token (al) and then () with their decoded forms.

title: Count the Number of Consistent Strings
statement: Count words containing only characters present in allowed.
explanation: Build a set of allowed characters and reject a word on its first disallowed character.

title: Count of Matches in Tournament
statement: Return the number of matches needed to determine a winner among n teams.
explanation: Every match eliminates exactly one team, so n teams require n-1 matches.

title: Determine if String Halves Are Alike
statement: Return true when the first and second halves contain the same number of vowels.
explanation: Count vowels in each half and compare the totals.

title: Maximum Units on a Truck
approach: Load highest units per box first
statement: Maximize units loaded while respecting the truck's box capacity.
explanation: Sort box types by units per box descending and greedily load as many as fit.

title: Decode XORed Array
approach: Recover each next value using XOR
statement: Given encoded[i]=arr[i] XOR arr[i+1] and arr[0], reconstruct arr.
explanation: Each next element is the previous decoded element XOR encoded[i].

title: Find the Highest Altitude
statement: Return the maximum altitude reached from initial altitude zero.
explanation: Accumulate each gain and track the maximum prefix altitude, including the initial zero.
